areas.title: Merging is safe before either mode ships: no replay of another task's work, only the reviewed version is merged, a waiting merge is kept and retried, dependent branches stay true, merge commits only, and never around the person's rules
problems: [blocker] The merge step replays a branch that carries another task's work. When main moved it rebases the PR branch (packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:243 `git.rebaseOnto(base)`) and force-pushes it (:252). A dependent task's branch is built by merging its dependencies' unmerged branches in (packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:322-349, DEPS_BASE_REF :129; its own comment :323-324: 'a rebase would copy that work into the branch as new commits'). The rebase copies the dependency's commits: its own commits never reach main, GitHub never marks its PR merged, and merging it later is an add/add conflict (research challenge's local run; /tmp/frbench/owner-q/gitexp). continueResolved does the same rebase after a resolved conflict (pr-executor.ts:691).

[blocker] The reviewed version is not saved. ReviewedPrMerge.mergeReviewed takes 'the reviewed commit' to be the task worktree's HEAD when it runs (merge.ts:376-381); its own rebase moves that HEAD and force-pushes (merge.ts:240-256). A retry after a rebase, or after a crash in the middle of one, would merge a commit the critic never saw.

[blocker] A waiting merge is lost. A merge whose checks still run after DEFAULT_CHECKS_WAIT_MS (merge.ts:54, :305-312) files a card and writes only the task's reason text (merge.ts:524-527); nothing retries it when the checks turn green (the watcher only starts a session on an all-green head, githost-watcher.ts:22-40), and nothing is kept when the PC sleeps or the app closes between the critic's accept and the merge (runner.ts:1888-1903 calls the merge inline; there is no durable marker). 'unverified' and 'not_allowed' file no card at all (merge.ts ASKS_HUMAN :590-596).

[blocker] The dependent-branch fix (fix/decisions cb39188, ADR 0106 point 6) leaves gaps and says something untrue. Every dependent PR says 'Merge in any order.' (pr-executor.ts:152-156), which holds only for GitHub's 'Create a merge commit' (squash-merging either PR first conflicts when the dependent edited the dependency's file: /tmp/frbench/owner-q/gitexp). A dependency whose PR is closed unmerged, or whose task is redone or cancelled, stays inside the dependent branch (unmergedDependencies :447-473 skips closed PRs, but the branch already holds the commits from :346-349) and reaches main with it, unseen. A dependency merged by any method does not rebuild the dependent branch (no code), so its PR keeps listing the dependency's files.

[major] Squash is the default: GitHubHost.mergePullRequest sends merge_method 'squash' unless told otherwise (packages/capabilities/src/githost/github.ts:425) and the merge step never says (merge.ts:315-318, input built at :427 without method); the in-memory host ignores the method (memory.ts:203-225). The owner merged forerunner-sandbox #4 with a merge commit.

[major] Nothing reads the branch's rules: the merge uses the plain endpoint (github.ts:418-439). GitHub does not let a PR's author (Forerunner opens PRs with the person's own token) approve it; admins are exempt from classic branch protection by default; and merging a dependent PR marks its dependency merged 'even when branch protection rules were not satisfied' (GitHub docs, about pull request merges). An automatic merge, or an admin token, can go around the person's own rules.

[major] A redo of a task whose PR was merged or closed reuses its branch name (pr-executor.ts:273-276; task.branch is kept on reopen) and looks for open PRs only (:314-317). With 'delete branch on merge' off (forerunner-sandbox), the old branch is still on GitHub, so the redo's push is not a fast-forward and is refused (read in the code, not run).

[minor] When main moved after the review on a repository with no automatic checks, nothing checks the combined result before an automatic merge: the merge step asks again only for the checks the reviewed head had (merge.ts:240-260, :292-304), so with none it merges at once (forerunner-sandbox has no workflows).
decisions: merging: GitHub projects: default 'you press Merge' with a one-click Merge in the app (dependency order, merge commits only, the safe merge step); per-project option 'merge automatically after review'; 'Take this work out' (revert PR naming later tasks that built on it). Each task's agent keeps committing on its own branch.
root_causes: packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts mergeChecked (:222-262) always rebases a moved base, whatever the branch holds; pr-executor.ts keeps a merged-in branch current by merging (mergeMoved :530-549), but the merge step and continueResolved (:691) do not know that.
merge.ts reads the reviewed commit from the worktree at merge time (:376-381); the critic's accept writes no commit anywhere.

There is no durable merge state: MergeOutcome lives in the session's memory and the task's reason text (merge.ts:505-534); packages/state has no merge record, and the session waits up to 10 minutes inline (merge.ts:54) as the only chance.

pr-executor.ts unmergedDependencies (:447-473) decides once per run what to merge in; nothing reacts when a dependency's PR is merged, closed or redone (githost-watcher.ts marks a closed PR and stops reading it, :468-469).
github.ts:425 defaults to 'squash'; merge.ts passes no method; GitHost (types.ts:209-260) has no way to read a branch's rules or a merged PR's merge commit.
areas.fix_scope: Engine only; the per-project setting and the in-app Merge are 'merge-in-app', the PC's copy, preview and take-out are 'merged-work'. (1) A durable merge record per task in packages/state (a migration; reviewed head sha, state waiting_checks | queued | ready | merged | left_to_you, merge sha, method, attempts, last sentence, updated_at), written by ReviewedPrMerge on its first call after an accept (the worktree's HEAD is then the reviewed commit, before any rebase) and pinned from then on: every merge uses the record's sha, never the worktree's HEAD. A task with no record (accepted before this change, or a crash before the record) is never merged automatically; it waits for the person's Merge. (2) No replay: a branch that holds merged-in work (DEPS_BASE_REF set, or merges since the base: git.hasMergesSince) is never rebased, in merge.ts and in continueResolved; main is merged into it (git.mergeFrom) when that merges cleanly, and once every dependency is in main the branch is rebuilt onto main from refs/forerunner/deps-base (git rebase --onto origin/<base> DEPS_BASE_REF), so its PR holds only its own commits; a branch with no merged-in work may still be rebased. After main was merged in or the branch rebuilt, the record's reviewed version moves only if the task's own change (the diff from DEPS_BASE_REF) is unchanged; otherwise the PR waits for the person. (3) Persist and retry: a merge that waits (checks running, a merge queue that took it, the session ending, sleep, a crash) keeps its record; the watcher's poll retries records whose checks turned green, and the daemon's start resumes records left half-way, with no session running; each retry re-reads the PR head against the record. A merge left to the person always carries one sentence on the record (no silent not_allowed or unverified). (4) Dependent branches: when a dependency's PR is merged (any method, in the app or on GitHub: the watcher sees it merged), the dependent branch is rebuilt onto main as in (2) and its PR body updated; when a dependency's PR is closed unmerged, or its task is redone or cancelled, the dependent branch is rebuilt without it, and when its own work needs it (the rebuild conflicts) one card names the PR in words. Until a dependent is rebuilt its PR says 'Builds on #4 (not merged yet): this pull request includes its changes. Merge #4 first, or use Merge in Forerunner, which merges them in order.' Never 'Merge in any order'. (5) Merge commits only: every merge Forerunner makes sends merge_method 'merge' pinned to the reviewed sha; a repository that does not allow merge commits (allow_merge_commit false; getRepo does not read it today, github.ts:293-316) is never merged by Forerunner, with one sentence; the in-memory and testenv hosts honour the method. (6) The safe merge request: before any merge read the branch's rules (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{b}, and the classic protection when readable) through a new GitHost method; when a rule requires approving reviews, a code owner's review, or anything Forerunner cannot satisfy, Forerunner does not merge (neither automatically nor on the person's click) and the record says why in one sentence ('This repository needs an approving review before merging, and GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request: merge it on GitHub once someone else approved it.'); never an admin bypass. Use GitHub's asynchronous merge with bypass_rules false only after checking its documentation (it is not in /tmp/frbench/owner-q/docs; unverified); otherwise the plain endpoint pinned to the sha after the rules check. (7) The automatic mode ('merge-in-app''s setting) merges only when main has not moved since the review, or the repository's checks ran green on the updated head; otherwise that PR waits for the person's Merge with one sentence. (8) A redo of a task whose PR was merged or closed starts from main on a fresh branch name. (9) One callback when a task's PR becomes merged (in the app, automatically, or seen merged on GitHub by the watcher, with the merge sha read from the PR): 'merged-work' wires the copy refresh, the preview cleanup and 'Take this work out' to it; 'merge-in-app' reads the record for its words. (10) A new ADR (next free number at merge time) amending ADR 0062 and ADR 0106 point 6; docs/maintainers/runtime.md, capabilities.md, state.md; docs/user-guide.md (repository section); CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. Leave room for wave 8: the record is per task and per install; sharing it between installs is the collaboration module's.

areas.title: A budget stop is a clean pause in the engine: Claude Code really stops and is counted once, the agent hears an 80% wrap-up on both paths, a run that wrapped up is 'paused' (no review, no failed try), the stop names its real limit, and a run cannot eat the review share
problems: [blocker] On the subscription a budget stop does not stop Claude Code. Forerunner's check throws inside the message loop (packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:285-289); the stream is closed only when the run was aborted (:322-328), and nothing aborts it on this path; unregister() (:365) takes the run off the kill switch (enforcement/killswitch.ts:121-123), so Stop now can no longer reach it, and the hooks still allow tools after run() returned (packages/runtime/test/sdk-driver.test.ts:117-133). Claude Code can go on editing the task's folder and using the plan allowance, uncounted, until its own maxBudgetUsd (:206), maxTurns (60) or the end (read in the code and the SDK bundle; not run).

[blocker] Subscription usage is counted wrongly: every assistant message's usage is added (sdk.ts:255-283), while messages of parallel tool calls share one id and one usage and a message's output_tokens is a placeholder (Agent SDK cost-tracking docs): input counted twice, output too low, so an 80% line would fire at the wrong time.

[major] The agent is never told about its budget: the 80% 'finish current' decision is only a warning event (agent/loop.ts:371-378); the model starts new work until the call that would go over is refused (enforcement/budget.ts:103-125).

[major] A graceful wrap-up would read as done: a run that ends normally is 'completed', mapped to 'done' (session/executor.ts:1257-1269), reviewed by the critic (review money), rejected for unmet criteria and counted as a failed try on the ladder.

[major] The run's last words are dropped at a budget stop: an error always replaces the report in the run's artifacts (executor.ts:1289-1297), so the next run reads 'It failed: The run failed: run budget would be exceeded' (task-context.ts:198-207).

[major] The real limit is not named: a stop at the month cap, the project cap or the subscription allowance (hooks.ts:156-169 throw budget_exceeded with details.level) goes down the task-budget path whenever the task's cap is below the session's (executor.ts:1331), so its card offers 'Raise the budget', which does not help; on the subscription Claude Code's own error_max_budget_usd result reads as provider_error (sdk.ts:305-311): Failed, retried as a passing glitch (read in the code, not reproduced).

[major] A running task can eat the share kept for reviews: the run's cap is the smaller of the task's cap and what the whole session has left (executor.ts:791, :824 use budget.remainingUsdMicro()), and budget.ts:139-152 lets the current call run past the work ceiling; the task's review then has no money (packages/critic/src/critic.ts, phase 'review').
decisions: budgets: Q3 yes: 80/20 wrap-up per run, paused outcome (no review, no failed try), code-side save with 'where I stopped / left to do', resume from it, card naming the real limit with 'Continue (CHF N more)' starting the next session at once, cancel sets work aside and names stuck dependents, subscription stop really stops Claude Code, better estimates and caching.
root_causes: sdk.ts handles Forerunner's refusal as an exception that ends its for-await loop, not as an abort of the Claude Code process; the iterator keeps running unless the controller was aborted.
sdk.ts sums usage per assistant message instead of per message id, and never takes output tokens from the result message.
SessionBudget.precheck (budget.ts:103-152) has one 80% line for the session and none per run; the hooks return finish_current, but the loop and the SDK driver only log it.
The executor maps outcomes from the driver's outcome only (executor.ts:1257-1269) and keeps the error over the report (:1289-1297); it reads the cap's source (runCapOf) but not the refusal's level.
executor.ts:791 uses the session's whole remainder, not its work budget (the cap less reserveShare).
areas.fix_scope: (1) The subscription first: on every budget stop (Forerunner's refusal, Claude Code's own error_max_budget_usd, the run cap) abort the run's controller and wait until Claude Code has exited (bounded; then the process is ended) before the run returns; the run stays registered with the kill switch until then; the run's token is marked ended so the hooks refuse every tool after the stop; count usage once per message id and take output tokens from the result message; maxBudgetUsd slightly above the run cap so Forerunner's own stop comes first; error_max_budget_usd reads as budget_exceeded. Prove it with a fake SDK that keeps sending messages and tool calls after the stop. (2) The 80% line per run: SessionBudget gets a per-run work line at 80% of the run's cap, the reserve being the larger of 20% and the worst-case cost of two calls (budget.ts already computes the worst case; 'cost' owns the price of a call); the hooks return 'wrap_up' once. (3) The wrap-up message on both paths: the loop adds one text block after the last tool results (never inside a tool result): 'About a fifth of this task's budget is left. Start nothing new, leave the files working, and end your report with Where I stopped: and Left to do: as a list.'; the SDK path returns the same text once as additionalContext from PostToolUse. The brief says what those two headings are for. (4) 'Paused': a run that ended after the wrap-up message, or with a 'Left to do:' list, or at a budget stop, has the outcome 'paused': no critic, no failed try; its report is kept (the error goes beside it, not over it) and parsed into the run's artifacts as { handoff: { stopped, leftToDo } }, data only (JSON-quoted when read back; it may carry web text); the runner routes 'paused' to today's budget card until 'budget-resume' replaces it; the Run row keeps outcome 'budget_exceeded', so 'cost''s learner skips it. (5) The real limit: the stop carries its level (the task's budget, the specialist's limit, the session, the project, the month, the subscription allowance) from the refusal's details into budgetStop.source, and the run's sentence names it ('stopped at this month's cap of CHF 150'); 'budget-resume''s card uses it. (6) A run's cap is at most what is left of the session's work budget (executor.ts:791, :824), so the review share stays for reviews. (7) A new ADR amending ADR 0105 (the pause; with today's review share about 0.8 x 0.8 = 64% of a session goes to work, as the owner was told), docs/maintainers/runtime.md, the user guide's budget text, CHANGELOG.

Cap: USD 4.00 in total, stopping at a clean point if it is reached. (2) Credentials, about USD 0.20: a bench home whose only credential is a key-shaped invalid API key written to the bench's file vault (setup refuses an invalid key, so the vault is written directly): a one-task brief gives one card 'Anthropic refused your API key' and the task waits, no failed-task cards; saving the real key in Settings clears the mark and the task starts by itself; the plan card of a research brief says where it runs and why. (5) Costs, about USD 0.40: the live smoke journey (smoke.cjs --live) on a fresh bench: each task's real cost within about x2 of the plan card's estimate per kind; specialist calls after the first show cache reads. (6) The window: the Desktop app workflow's window check on Windows with the Ctrl+click on Inbox showing the Inbox (no model cost). Reserve about USD 0.80 for one retry.
